history.recommendation_text: The Board recommends that the Administration consult with troop-contributing countries to reconsider the deployment of a unit if the military performance evaluation task force identifies a lack of predefined basic military skills during predeployment visits.
history.administration_response: The Administration stated that in all identified cases of a lack of basic military skills, the Administration had consulted with affected troop- and police- contributing countries. The initial deployment or rotation had been delayed to allow the troop-contributing country to rectify the identified shortfalls and implement the concrete recommendations provided by the military performance evaluation task force. In three cases, the Administration conducted additional predeployment visits. Any lack of necessary basic military skills was reported by the military performance evaluation task force during the structured monthly performance meeting process in the Department of Peace Operations and triggered, depending on the severity of identified shortfalls, consultations on a political and/or military level with affected troop- and police-contributing countries.
history.board_assessment: As shown by the number and gravity of the shortcomings MINUSMA has identified (see chap. II of the present report), the Board holds that the Administration needs to strengthen its efforts to ensure that troop- and police-contributing countries reconsider deployment in cases of a lack of predefined basic military skills. This recommendation remains under implementation.

history.recommendation_text: In paragraph 117 of its report, the Board recommended that the Administration consult with troop-contributing countries to reconsider deployment of a unit if the military performance evaluation task force identifies a lack of predefined basic military skills during predeployment visits.
history.reference_raw: Recommendations contained in the report of the Board of Auditors for the 12 -month period ended 30 Jun e 2019 ( A/74/5 (Vol. II)
history.sg_progress: The process for predeployment visits, as recommended by the Board, has in fact been implemented in line with the Integrated Peacekeeping Performance and Accountability Framework and the operational readiness assurance and performance improvement policy. The Administration would also like to note that military units with performance shortfalls identified during a mission are validated during the predeployment visit conducted for the next rotation of the contingent. The focus of this validation is to identify the contingent’s readiness for deployment and also to prioritize remediation in collaboration with troop-contributing countries and strategic partners, in line with Security Council resolution 2436 (2018), in which the Council requested the Secretary-General to help troop-contributing countries meet United Nations performance standards. Troop-contributing countries have responded positively to recommendations made by the military performance evaluation task force whenever shortfalls of military skills have been identified during predeployment visits. In 2020, one unit with identified shortfalls was not allowed to be deployed until all remedial measures and improvement recommendations had been implemented. As these established processes continue to be maintained, the Administration requests the closure of this recommendation by the Board.
